en: to be hosted; to be held

examples.en: The Olympics are held every four years.

examples.ko: 다음 달에 큰 음악회가 개최될 예정이에요.
examples.en: A big concert is scheduled to be held next month.
The meeting was held in Seoul.
A thousand people came to the event that was held.
If it rains, the event won't be held.
I'm waiting for the day the festival is held.

explain: 큰 행사·대회·회의가 열릴 때 쓰는 공식적인 말이에요. 작은 모임에는 '열리다'를 써요. 파티가 '개최되다'라고 하면 너무 거창해요. 주최하는 쪽은 '개최하다'예요.
explain_en: A formal word for big events, contests and conferences. For small gatherings use '열리다'; saying a party is '개최되다' sounds grand. The organizer side is '개최하다'.

dis.h: an event is held at a time or place

p.n: 주관되다 says who organizes or runs the event, so it doesn't fit with a place.

examples.ko: 그 가수의 내한 소식에 팬들이 들떠 있어요.
examples.en: Fans are excited by the news of that singer's visit to Korea.

examples.ko: 내한 공연 표는 오 분 만에 매진됐어요.
examples.en: Tickets for the concert in Korea sold out in five minutes.
I heard this is their first visit to Korea.
The press conference for the Korea visit is tomorrow afternoon.

examples.ko: 내한 일정 중에 한식도 먹는다고 해요.
examples.en: They say they will eat Korean food during their Korea schedule.
Many bands are scheduled to visit Korea this year.

explain: 공연자나 스포츠 선수처럼 외국 사람이 한국에 올 때 써요. 대통령 같은 정상이나 공식 손님이 올 때는 '방한'을 더 많이 써요. 보통 '내한 공연'처럼 명사 앞에서 써요.
explain_en: Use it when a foreign performer or athlete comes to Korea. For heads of state or official guests, 방한 is more common. It is usually placed before a noun, as in 내한 공연.

examples.en: A famous band is coming to Korea next month.

examples.ko: 그 배우는 영화 홍보를 위해 내한했어요.
examples.en: That actor came to Korea to promote a movie.
Every time they come to Korea, they hold a fan meeting.
It's a singer's first visit to Korea, so expectations are high.

examples.ko: 내한하면 꼭 가 보고 싶은 곳이 있대요.
examples.en: They say there's a place they definitely want to visit when they come to Korea.
The players who came to Korea took photos at the airport.

explain: 내한하다는 외국 사람이 한국에 오는 것만 말해서 한국 사람에게는 쓰지 않아요. 한국에 오는 연예인을 말할 때 자주 써요. 같은 상황에서 일반 여행자에게는 '한국에 오다/방문하다'가 자연스러워요.
explain_en: 내한하다 is only for foreigners coming to Korea, never for Korean people. It is common for entertainers arriving in Korea. For an ordinary traveler, 한국에 오다 or 방문하다 sounds more natural.

examples.en: The flu spreads widely every winter.
This song was a huge hit last year.

examples.ko: 요즘 이 게임이 대유행이라서 다들 해요.
examples.en: This game is a huge craze these days, so everyone plays it.
The school closed because of the outbreak.
That hairstyle was a huge fad for a while.
A worldwide outbreak has begun.

explain: 그냥 '유행'보다 훨씬 크게 퍼진다는 느낌이에요. 노래나 옷 같은 유행에도 쓰고, 병이 크게 퍼질 때도 써요. 보통 '대유행이다, 대유행을 하다'로 말해요.
explain_en: It feels much bigger than plain '유행' (trend). You can use it for trends like songs and clothes, and also when a disease spreads widely. It is usually said as '대유행이다' or '대유행을 하다'.

examples.en: I had a dream about pigs last night.
I bought a lottery ticket the day I dreamed about pigs.

examples.ko: 돼지꿈은 재물운이 있다는 뜻으로 많이 말해요.
examples.en: People often say a pig dream means good fortune with money.

examples.ko: 돼지꿈 덕분인지 오늘 일이 잘 풀려요.
examples.en: Maybe thanks to the pig dream, things are going well today.
My friend laughed while telling me about a pig dream.

examples.ko: 돼지꿈이라서 기분이 좋았는데 아무 일도 없었어요.
examples.en: I was happy because it was a pig dream, but nothing happened.

explain: 한국에서는 돼지꿈을 복이나 재물이 들어오는 좋은 꿈으로 여기는 믿음이 있어요. 그래서 돼지꿈을 꾸면 복권을 사 보는 사람도 있어요. '돼지꿈을 꾸다'라고 말해요.
explain_en: In Korea there is a belief that a pig dream is a good dream that brings luck or wealth. Some people even buy a lottery ticket after having one. You say '돼지꿈을 꾸다'.

examples.en: Our family celebrates the holidays together.
We celebrated the birthday quietly with just family.
I went down to my hometown to celebrate the New Year.
The way of celebrating Chuseok differs from house to house.

examples.ko: 명절을 쇠고 나니 몸이 많이 피곤해요.
examples.en: After celebrating the holiday, I feel very tired.

examples.ko: 이사 때문에 올해는 설을 쇠지 못할 것 같아요.
examples.en: Because of the move, I may not be able to celebrate the New Year this year.

explain: '설을 쇠다', '생일을 쇠다'처럼 명절·생일·기념일과 같이 써요. '보내다'는 그 시간을 지낸다는 말이고, 쇠다는 그날의 행사를 챙긴다는 느낌이에요. '생일을 챙기다'와 비슷하게 쓰는 경우가 많아요.
explain_en: It pairs with holidays, birthdays, and anniversaries, as in '설을 쇠다' and '생일을 쇠다'. '보내다' just means spending the time; 쇠다 means carrying out the day's customs. It is often used much like '생일을 챙기다'.

examples.ko: 이 수필집은 작년에 출판됐는데 아직도 잘 팔려요.
examples.en: This essay collection was published last year and still sells well.

examples.ko: 좋아하는 작가의 수필집을 한 권 샀어요.
examples.en: I bought a collection of essays by my favorite author.
Reading the essay collection put my mind at ease.
I browsed the essay collection section at the library.
I heard our teacher is publishing a first essay collection.

examples.ko: 이 수필집에는 여행하면서 쓴 글이 많아요.
examples.en: This essay collection has many pieces written while traveling.

explain: '시집', '소설집'처럼 '~집'이 붙어 글을 모은 책을 가리켜요. 서점에서는 '에세이'라는 말을 더 많이 써서 '에세이 코너'로 불러요. 책은 '수필집을 내다/펴내다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Like '시집' (poetry collection) and '소설집' (story collection), the '~집' ending marks a book that gathers pieces of writing. Bookstores more often say '에세이', so the shelf is called the '에세이 코너'. You publish one with '수필집을 내다/펴내다'.

examples.ko: 이 팀은 올해 승률이 아주 높아요.
examples.en: This team has a very high win rate this year.
As the win rate went up, fans increased.
Our team's win rate is sixty percent.
I practice every day to raise my win rate.

examples.ko: 지난 시즌 승률보다 올해가 더 좋아요.
examples.en: This year is better than last season's win rate.
The coach did not obsess only over the win rate.

explain: '승률'은 이긴 횟수를 전체 경기 수로 나눈 비율이에요. 야구, 축구, 게임 이야기에서 '승률이 높다/낮다'처럼 많이 써요.
explain_en: 승률 is the share of games won out of all games played. It comes up in baseball, soccer, and gaming as '승률이 높다/낮다'.

examples.en: The drama I liked ended yesterday.

examples.ko: 그 프로그램은 십 년 만에 종영하게 됐어요.
examples.en: That program is ending after ten years.

examples.ko: 드라마가 종영하면 배우들이 같이 여행을 간대요.
examples.en: I heard the actors go on a trip together when the drama ends.

examples.ko: 다음 주에 종영하는 예능을 놓치지 마세요.
examples.en: Don't miss the variety show that ends next week.

examples.ko: 방송국은 시청률이 낮아서 일찍 종영하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The broadcaster decided to end it early because of low ratings.

examples.ko: 종영한 뒤에도 그 노래는 계속 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: Even after the show ended, that song is still very popular.

explain: 드라마나 예능 같은 방송 프로그램이 마지막 회로 끝날 때 써요. 영화나 공연이 끝나는 건 '막을 내리다'나 '상영이 끝나다'라고 해요. 시작은 '방영하다', '첫 방송'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is used when a TV program such as a drama or variety show finishes with its last episode. For a movie or show closing, Koreans say 막을 내리다 or 상영이 끝나다. The start is 방영하다 or 첫 방송.
